utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I do understand that there are no preliminaries. While the witness is escorted into the courtroom, I'd like to use the time to deal briefly with a matter, and it's the Prosecution's motion to substitute proposed expert Ols with Curtis. On the 13th of April of this year, the Defence filed its response to the Prosecution motion to amend its Rule 65 ter witness list to substitute Martin Ols, RM625, with colleague Timothy Curtis, which was filed on the 25th of March. The Defence does not oppose the proposed substitution of these two witnesses but notes in its response that it is still awaiting additional information and material relating to the report tendered for Witness Ols which is the same report the Prosecution intends to tender with proposed witness Curtis. Given that the Defence does not object to the substitution, the Chamber hereby grants the addition of Timothy Curtis to the Rule 65 ter witness list, and confirms the withdrawal of Martin Ols. The Prosecution is consequently instructed to file a Rule 65 ter summary for Witness Curtis. The Chamber recalls that in its 9th of November, 2012, decision it found that Ols was sufficiently qualified to testify as an expert witness. Upon review of Witness Curtis's CV contained in an annex to the Prosecution's motion to substitute him for Ols, the Chamber is satisfied of his expertise, noting, in particular, the fact that he was a signatory of the tendered report. The Chamber further recalls that in its decision of the 9th of November, 2012, it had decided that Ols cannot be called for at least 30 days from the date that the Defence received further information and material specified in paragraph 10 of the Chamber's decision, relating to the applied methodology in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Similarly, Witness Curtis may be called at the earliest 30 days from the date that the Prosecution has provided all the relevant material to the Defence. Is the Prosecution already in a position to give an indication as to when it anticipates completing the disclosure of the requested additional information and materials to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. We just received that information and we have copied it, and we are meeting with the Defence over coffee this afternoon to discuss the other matters, and we'll provide it to them this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Ruez, it is not very polite to continue speaking when you enter the courtroom. Apologies for that. We were dealing with another matter. We'll continue, but may I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. I was informed that you would like to have your glasses which have you not brought with you. If there would be any way to -- that we can assist to get them, we'll be happy to do so. And, otherwise, we might be a bit more patient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a small selection of glasses which sometimes help witnesses, so we'll give you our series of what we have and then let's see whether it helps or not. Please do not hesitate to ask for further assistance, if needed. I'll put on my glasses ... Yes, I see Mr. Mladic has some glasses left which I do not know whether they have the proper size. I take it that it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I could do without and we can sort that out during the next recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. During the next break we'll further deal with the glasses. Mr. McCloskey, if you're ready, please continue your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I would like to begin by offering the short helicopter overflight video we saw, 65 ter 22313A, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 22313A receives number P1128, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed. Could you please repeat --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number was P1128.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1128 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we will continue with your chronology of photos and exhibits. If we go to e-court page 20. It's where we left off, and it's exhibit number 28756. And this is in your chapter entitled: "Srebrenica town." It's page 2 in the -- in the book -- in your book, Mr. Ruez, but you'll see it on the screen. Now, we can -- some of these, as you know, are more self-explanatory than others and so we can go through them. And that's page 20 in e-court. We can go through them with your comments. Some will obviously be more than others. This first shot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This first shot is only a still photograph showing the arrival when coming from Zeleni Jadar and on the first hill overlooking Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 21 in e-court, the next page, page 3 in the book.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this view is also a still picture so -- of a better quality, showing the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. This is a map graphic.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one is -- indicates one of the two courses of action that the population -- yeah, the population inside the enclave took on 11 July. Since during the previous days most of the people had assembled around the Bravo Company in Srebrenica town, on 11 July, once it was realised that UN air-strikes that were supposed to stop the attack were a failure, the decision was made for these men who decided to flee to take the direction of the north of the enclave and assemble together in an area of a village named Susnjari which is circled with the green dots.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. And this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the second movement, the second option that the population took. So all the women, the children, the elderly, but also an amount of men who did not want to try to escape through the forest decided to move from Srebrenica town and find shelter in and around the UN base, the main base, which was in Potocari, approximately 5 kilometres north of Srebrenica town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see a grey perimeter going around Srebrenica with yellow dots and letters. Can you just briefly explain what that is.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These dots mark the positions of the UN observation posts which were positioned on the so-called border of the enclave but there was no borders at this enclave. It's rough positions of -- of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the next page which you refer to as Potocari. And we now have an aerial image. Can you briefly explain where we got this aerial image. And we see yellow markings and we see black and white printing in blocks. Could you explain, as you can, what this means?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These -- these are aerial pictures. This one as well as the other ones in the book were provided by the US State Department. All markings on these pictures in white are the markings originally made by the provider, in this case, overview Potocari, Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the date, 13 July 1995. This markings were initially on the picture. The yellow markings are markings that I added to the picture in order to pin-point the main structures witnesses refer to when it comes to describe the situation in Potocari during the 12 and the 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we -- we see the -- the yellow markings. You made those personally?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the Court has heard about the UN base and the White House so I don't think we need you to mention those at this point. The other places that you have marked, what was the significance of the others, the express bus compound, the other buildings?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the people arrived in Potocari in the evening of the 11, where they spent also the 12, the night between the 12 and the 13, since the evacuation was totally finished the 13, the people found shelter for some of them inside the UN base, but once this base was full they had to find shelter elsewhere. So they found shelter mainly in the express bus compound facility, the zinc factory and the Energoinvest, otherwise called the 11 of March factory. So the witnesses, most of them refer to these buildings. But others were also spending the night outside or in houses but as close as possible always to the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And were you yourself on the ground in Potocari at various times during the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. Overview Potocari, is up south or is up north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This one is direction south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact, I showed each time precise what is the direction of the photograph because sometimes, indeed, it is south rather than north. This one is looking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- towards the south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's say, common is to have north at the top --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but on this page it's just the opposite.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Reversed, absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So if we could go to page 25 in e-court and this is a -- what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this one is -- shows more or less the same things than the other one but this one is looking in the good direction; that is, north. And you can easily now recognise not only the UN base, have another assessment of the distance between the UN base and the White House, but also see that the factories we were talking about are in a very close perimeter. At the right of the White House, you have the -- the express bus compound. And then you have also the zinc factory with the blue roof. And a bit above it, bottom left of the zinc factory you have the 11th of March factory. The interest of this one is also -- when you look at the circle around the White House, the line at the bottom of the circle positions also where was the separation line where the UN soldiers were positioned, the Bosnian Serb soldiers were positioned. The people went through this line at that location and that's where the separation process took place. Women and children, elderly put aside, and -- and in buses, and the men taken to the White House. It's where the big tree -- the big tree just at the bottom of the White House.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I do encourage Your Honours, I know you will ask questions, because we will try to move this along because you have seen evidence already on some of this, as you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let go to the next -- the next page, 26 in e-court. We see snow on the ground. Tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture was taken end of January 1996. It was the first opportunity for me to access to the territory of the Republika Srpska. Thanks to a visit that was made there by Mr. John Shattuck, who was under-secretary of state for human rights and who wanted to go to Republika Srpska, to Nova Kasaba, in order to show that there was freedom of movement implemented since the Dayton Agreements. So there were press waiting there. But we left from Belgrade for this mission, and Mr. Shattuck accepted, in fact, to transform the mission as a kind of fact-finding mission for me and a colleague who was with me so that we could visit a few sites we absolutely wanted to -- to locate and use this opportunity. So we could go to the -- the school of Orahovac. We could go to the soccer field at Nova Kasaba. We could stop at Glogova and could also have this stop in Potocari, so this is why there is snow on the ground in this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What is this on page 26 in e-court, page 8 in your book?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is one of the most important structure in Potocari since it is the house where the men who were separated from the others were taken to, and from this house, once the house was full, the men were taken on board of buses and driven to Bratunac. This house was visited by UN military observer, Major Kingori, who, when he was interviewed, claimed that on this spot he was present with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another view of -- of the house. This witness I referred to said that this house was totally full. People were compressed inside, and it was so full that some were even also on the balcony. We had access to a video filmed by Zoran Petrovic at the time of the events, but this independent journalist had erased from his film some important parts which provided interesting information. Among the pieces that he had erased from his film is this very short view of men sitting on a balcony, and as you can see, you can see the bars of this balcony. They match perfectly the ones of this extract of the Zoran Petrovic video. So these are photographs of men at the White House. So prisoners at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we will have an investigator that will talk in much more depth about the -- the two Petrovic videos, the one that had the missing parts, and then the missing parts. But briefly, Mr. Ruez, while you were still an investigator here, had the missing parts been available to you and had they appeared yet?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We knew they were of fundamental importance since would they not be, this journalist would have had no need to erase them but they were only accessible to the OTP after my departure in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we can see in this still this circle upon circles and it says "B." Can you tell us what that says from your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the logo and the name of independent television in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you explain where this -- just very briefly where these -- these lost clips, if I would call them that, came from. How -- how did they appear? Were they played over something?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were played -- they were -- they were played in Belgrade once. I think before the cuts. But during years we -- despite of many efforts, we could never put a hand on an original recording of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to go back now to the -- the trial video, 65 ter 28780, which does contain the -- both the original Petrovic video that Mr. Ruez had without the -- without the missing cuts. And then we have, as you will see, overlayed the missing cut that we see the still from. And if you could watch this. It's 9:09 to 10:54, V000-9267.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There should be sound and some subtitling.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are clothings, bags, dumped by these men before entering the -- the White House. They had to abandon their belongings in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we are at 09:23:7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's Feros, just next to the UN main compound. So the abandoned bags. Here you see Major Kingori with a few other UN soldiers and a Serb interpreter, the man wearing a Kalashnikov and a blue flak jacket, which is not UN equipment. This blue flak jacket is Bosnian Serb equipment, a real one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you've mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. There seems to be a sound problem. Could we ... I'll speak a few words to see whether it is any better. It seems to have been resolved. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ruez. At 9:55:4, can you -- you mention Major Kingori. Can you point him out for us so it's clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is at the left of the picture, turning his back to the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you can see Colonel Borovcanin, the head of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where precisely is Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't check there was any cut before, but in that case, it is in front of the White House.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which one so we know exactly --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right -- right in the middle of the picture, without a hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And that's at 9:59:5.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. So this is the entrance of the White House.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'll stop it here at 10:17:2. Can you explain why it went from the White House to this -- looks like a shell casing?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. It is the way Zoran Petrovic organised his film.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's continue to the next segment which is a new -- new Studio B segment, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So here is the site of the balcony with the men sitting on the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we're at 10:44:9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we heard at -- we end at 10:53:8. We heard a person speaking in Serbian and we saw lettering going on underneath. Can you tell us what that is, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I can say about this is to confirm that once I said in previous trial that Zoran Petrovic was, in my view, it is my purely personal opinion, not an independent journalist but a propagandist. I think that these comments are clear enough to explain the reason why I believe this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was that part of the -- this Studio B playback over Belgrade Television?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you for a second. We saw subtitling not in English, moving from the right to the left in the picture. We also saw subtitles in English, apparently reflecting the words spoken. You were talking about which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm talking only about the subtitles because I do not understand the local language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So we do not yet what we saw as far as the language, may I take it we'll most likely be B/C/S starting with Bambi or something of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can ask Mr. Ruez --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second, Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Ruez introduced a Mr. -- as his private personal opinion, not evidence, that he thought that Mr. Petrovic was a propagandist, rather. This witness comes as a witness of fact. We heard, or at least we read, the words spoken, that these were all registered criminals on the balcony. The personal views of this witness who is called as a witness of fact are not relevant. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we should be very careful anyhow that often you explain what we see, what it was. Sometimes I take it that you want to tell us that you think that it was A, B, or C, because you concluded that from statements given by other persons and combining that with what you saw on the ground. We have to be very careful where you are presenting facts you observed personally and where you explain, more or less summarise, what others said. Apart, of course, from adjudicated facts. That's a different area. But let's try not to mix it up. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for your information, the transcript, Mr. President, of the trial video actually has a translation of the -- of that part at English 76 through 77, and B/C/S 71 through 72. But perhaps Mr. Ruez will remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall back when you first saw this and that there was an advertisement for a -- or a mentioning of a Rolling Stones concert in Belgrade going along the bottom of that screen. Do you have any recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the simple answer then is: It's commercials. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let now go to the next page, which you basically note in a map graphic. We see a -- it's page 28 in e-court. And it's page 10 in your book but you'll see it on the screen. And down in the right corner we just see a black arrow. Briefly.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's the direction that was taken by these men who were separated into Potocari and moved to a very short distance from Potocari to the town of Bratunac. This happened starting the 12 and it continued the 13. The men -- so in -- in Potocari, direction Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. We see a blue arrow and a circle over the city of Bratunac. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows the direction from -- the picture is going -- it's north-west orientation, so the arrow shows the direction, the straight line coming from Potocari inside Bratunac town, and the interest of this picture is to show that Bratunac is a very small town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And we'll get into Bratunac in little more detail later. Let's go to the next picture. E-court 30. This is the beginning of a chapter that you call "Ex-filtration," and we see another black arrow from the Susnjari-Jaglici area across Nova Kasaba. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the men who assembled in Susnjari, these men were mainly of two groups, the 28th Division of BiH Army. The enclave had never been demilitarised despite of the agreements. These soldiers were armed. They were approximately 6.000 among a crowd of 15.000. The others were mainly unarmed but some had also weapons, and there was a very small army group at the end of this column. So we -- 28th Division went in front, first the -- all these people had to cross a minefield, so they opened a very small path. So it was a very slow process to get out of the area. It -- it took the night between the -- the 11 and the 12, and so this -- this column, I said it like an ant column, moved towards the collection of Konjevic Polje. The -- the black arrow is a rough indication. The real path is a bit underneath the Kravica river, because there is a steep hill just at the south of the -- of the strategic road going from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje where there is on top of this hill a power line, electrical power line, and this was the orientation for all the people, most of them who didn't knew the area. So they follow -- they had to follow this power line because this power line was going straight towards Konjevic Polje. Konjevic Polje is a very important location since it is the crossing point from this area to the area west, the limit being the road between Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba. As long as this road Konjevic Polje-Nova Kasaba was open, the column could go through, and this was the fate of the first group, the army. But once, on 13 in the morning, this was sealed by the Bosnian Serb army, the people were trapped in this area, so between Konjevic Polje and roughly the area of Kravica. So this elements on this map are very important to keep in mind because we will talk about these locations later on. And, also, I would like to point to you at the tip of this arrow, where the tip of the arrow is, is a big hill, and this hill is something that you will hear about also because it's from this hill that several witnesses could see events in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put a question at this point in time. Mr. Ruez, obviously you have not been present while the column was moving. What is the source of your knowledge about numbers of people in the column, the composition of the column, which part of the column was composed of soldiers, armed soldiers, and others? What is the source of your knowledge of all these details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is multiple sources. In fact, it's a combination of several witness statements from people who made this movement as well as the Bosnian Serb army. 6.000 armed men arrived alive in -- in Tuzla, members of the 28th Division. So army in front, people behind. It's -- it's an indication given by many -- many witnesses. And that the final result, as we know, as the Defence knows also, the main target of this operation fled, which is to say, the 28th Division. Most of it, let's say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When I ask you about -- when I ask you about your knowledge and your source, it's not necessary to refer to the knowledge of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a follow-up question. My question is: If your source is from a number of witnesses who were there, why do we hear you and not those witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could call in maybe 15 or 20 people rather than me just for this part. Because many of these people had nothing very important to say in terms of crimes committed. We interviewed a lot of people, and we didn't keep all of them as key witnesses, since this case quite quickly ended up focussing only on the main crimes. We had to disregard a lot of -- let's say, small criminal events. But at the beginning of the investigation, we were taking information from a lot of witnesses but without necessarily later on calling them as witnesses here for the trial because we didn't have, let's say, enough severe crimes to talk about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I remind you, Mr. McCloskey, of the best evidence rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. May I briefly respond so that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, before you do so, perhaps I add one observation. Mr. Ruez, when you're talking about "we," on the one-hand side, you say "we interviewed." That is a very factual thing you did. In the next line you say, "We did not keep them as key witnesses." That is the "we" who is making strategic and tactical decisions for the Prosecution. As I said before, I would like to have this all strictly separated. It started already yesterday with my first question, how do you know, and then you said, Well, of course, this is a conclusion because no soldier was there from UNPROFOR. Let's try to clearly distinguish facts -- the fact being Witness A told me this, Witness B told me that, Witness C told you that. Because these are facts that the witness told to you. And whether they are all three lying, or whether they're all three telling us the truth, or what you concluded on the basis of, et cetera, et cetera. There's a thin line here, Mr. McCloskey, between the Chamber drawing the conclusions on the basis of the evidence and a witness of fact drawing the conclusions on the basis of the evidence. And that is, I think, a concern which was expressed already by all three of the Judges until now and we're only one hour on our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could attempt to explain. When Mr. Ruez speaks, what -- what I believe -- the Prosecution takes it as what he is saying is the investigation has revealed that. And we -- the purpose of his testimony is in about five hours to give you, as he has said, a background of the chronology of the events and the places where it happened. We don't suggest that you're taking Mr. Ruez's word on -- on events. He is speaking of -- of witnesses that are either in this record in 92 bis or will testify. What he is trying to do is just give you an overall picture of these places and what the investigation revealed. And, as you can see, he also is -- mentions things that the Defence fully believe and the non-demilitarisation of the enclave, the presence of the 28th Division. In that regard, the Defence will see that we're not challenging those things. So he's really designed only in five hours to give you a background of what the investigation has revealed. It's hearsay. It's not necessarily for the truth of the matter he's asserted. I'm not sure any judgements have cited Mr. Ruez. He is here so that when the witnesses such as the one you saw yesterday comes to the soccer field, you have already seen the picture of the soccer field and the brief description. So that's all it is for, to give you a five-hour background of what the investigation revealed and the places. It is not meant to replace any evidence or witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed at this moment. And we do understand that most of the answers of Mr. Ruez should start, to begin with, with the investigation and the witnesses gave us the impression that this might have been the case. That is apparently -- and then we'll later, on the basis of the evidence, we'll see whether that impression will be the impression and the conclusion of the Chamber as well. Mr. Ruez, would you also carefully keep in mind when using your language not to tell us what happened but what you think has happened on the basis of your interviews of witnesses and going to the terrain. This is just a caveat for all of us, that we should try to present it for what it really is and to understand it for what it really is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. It's e-court 31. And you've got a -- a photograph and a yellow arrow. What has the investigation revealed that -- that allows you or causes you to put up this picture and this arrow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture really reveals nothing. It shows -- seen from in direction towards south at the bottom of the picture, the strategic road I was referring to previously with the two directions, and according to the knowledge I gained from these interviews, the alleged direction that these people took is marked on this map with this yellow arrow. So you can see the road, you can see bend going south of the hill, and these folks were walking on top just behind this hill, according to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the next page, just briefly what area is -- is this and what do you believe it depicts?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this depicts the big hill I was referring to previously, which is at the junction before Nova Kasaba and Konjevic Polje. This is the hill where some witnesses, I and other investigators, so we, think is the hill from where people could see events happening in Nova Kasaba, at Cerska valley, and at Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The next page. 33 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. So one is once you are on the hill but at the bottom of the hill, this is a picture I took as well as the other one, by the way, this is so the area the column had to cross, if willing, then to continue its way towards Muslim-held territory, and so there is an open space here, and you have to go to the opposite side and there is a road and a river. And at the right is the intersection of Konjevic Polje, going right would return to Bratunac, going left going south towards Nova Kasaba, and at the top of the picture, it's going along the Jadar river to the direction of Zvornik. The yellow arrow is indicating the movement this column was taking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we now on this picture facing south or north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This one is facing north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means the yellow dotted line indicates where you think, on the basis of the evidence of the -- on the testimonies, the statements of the witnesses, that they came from -- let me see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From Bratunac. And this is then where they had to cross the road --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- where you said there was a strategic issue involved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. The strategic blockade of the area that sealed the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's just for my orientation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let go to the next chapter entitled: "Surrender and arrest." And the next page is 34 on e-court, 16 in the book. And you have your first page, prisoners of war. And did the investigation identify various sites where Muslim men were assembled on 13 July?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you go to those sites you learned of and photograph them and put them in this book?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I take it -- tell us, these blue circles that we see on this page in front of us, what is that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These blue circles indicate the rough location of assembly points for captured men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And so let's now go through them. We can see that there's one off the page that didn't make it on the map, Luke. And let's go to the next page. It's 35 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. May I take it, although you didn't tell us, that the size of the circles is indicative for larger or smaller numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. But it is really a very, very rough --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- that's what I said indicative for larger or smaller numbers --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Otherwise I would have said indicative for the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So we're now at a page and we see a blue circle at Luke just off the map. So I -- I take it we're speaking of Luke at this point?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes absolutely. It's out of the map, unfortunately. Luke is the -- is a -- let's say, a little location just before reaching the front -- the confrontation line which at that place is named Kladanj. So the men who were -- I mean, the people who were taken on board of buses were shipped towards Kladanj where they had to finish the way by foot. But just before this, another separation took place, and the men who managed to get on board of these buses were later on -- I mean, at least one, the witness we know, they were separated here and taken, according to this man, to an elementary school. So we -- we were looking for this school in Tisca, in fact, which is on the map, but it was not in Tisca. We ended up going to Luke with this witness without whom we would not have found this very small elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page. 36 in e-court. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the location he describes. The orientation of this picture is roughly towards the west, so the -- the buses were taking this road towards this -- towards this direction but those who were separated were walked towards this small building. This is the building he showed us as being the building in which he was kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, 37. Is this the same building?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same building seen from the back. The vehicle was ours. In his initial interview, he said that he first he was in a group sitting in the -- on a meadow under a tree, and this is the -- this is the area where he said having sat with a group of others on 13 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12 July. I can't remember very well. 12 or 13. 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next picture. 38 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a classroom in which this witness claims having been taken to and where he was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This may be a good place to stop, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that. Beaten by who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Beaten by Bosnian Serb soldiers who were guarding the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will ... we will take a break of 20 minutes and resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I'll use the time to deal with a short procedural matter about MFI D203. Exhibit D203 was tendered through Witness Ekrem Suljevic on the 11th of February and subsequently marked for identification pending clarification of the translation. Source in the transcript is T8435. The Chamber notes the request of the Defence sent through informal communications on the 10th of April, 2013, to replace the English translation of D203 as it is currently in e-court with doc ID 0084-7435, with another English translation with doc ID 1D03-1079. I take it that replacement is to have a better translation or just another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have reviewed that new translation and have no objection to the replacement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber hereby requests you, Madam Registrar, to replace the current translation with doc ID 1D03-1079, and we admit D203 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could continue we should be at e-court page 39 of the -- of the book. Yeah. That's 38. Yes, 39. And we were at the -- what you have referred to as the regroupment sites, first one Luke. Now we see this page. What are the regroupment sites here briefly?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here are two -- two spots. One being Nova Kasaba, and the other one the soccer field of Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. We have an aerial image which is noted buses at a facility. And we see the yellow marks which we now know are marks that you put in. What have you identified here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture identifies the location that is the 65th Protection Regiment compound. It is a military facility in which Dutch UN peacekeeping personnel -- not Dutch and -- sorry, I'm reading the transcript. It's UN keeping [sic] personnel was held as well as, according to what they said, Bosnian prisoners. And on this aerial imagery one can see that there are buses also on the parking lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, have you been to this site yourself on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never entered the -- the military facility but we took a picture of it alongside of a road. You can see it's -- the short distance of the road at the right, top right of the picture, is the -- the road that goes from Bratunac towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you learn or -- or did you -- or do you recall was this a -- always a military facility or was it some civilian facility at some point, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about this. It was a military facility at the time of the events and shortly afterward, but I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a -- the same military facility but seen from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go on to the next page. And I -- I can tell you the -- the Judges have had some dealings with this so if you could just briefly explain -- explain this.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the picture says it, according to the provider, it shows a bus convoy but it is a still picture. We do not know if these buses are going towards the -- the evacuation point or driving back to Bratunac. This we don't know. What we can see on this picture is -- of interest is also the soccer field. The picture is taken 14 [sic] July approximately at 14 hours, at 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think -- take another look at the timing. I think you may have misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 14 hours; 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And then let's go to the next picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- could I ask the witness, which direction is what? To the right is going to ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the right is going towards Bratunac, so first to intersection of Konjevic Polje. And to the left, towards Nova Kasaba, Vlasenica and Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you considered the position of the buses on the road when you said that no -- that you do not know whether the buses are going in which direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We cannot say because it's a still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if -- if these buses were driving to the left of the picture, there were driving as if they were in England, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree. But on the other hand, we don't know if there are people are on board so it's -- their presence just shows that, indeed, on 13 July there were a lot of bus movements in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. But I think the parties could agree, I take it, that the buses --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are coming back, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether they are coming back or not, they are situated at the right-hand side of the road if you would look into the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They drive towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether they drive or not, I do not know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or not, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but they are situated on the right-hand side of the road in that direction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we see you have drawn yellow around this, concluding groups of prisoners and football field. And is that your conclusion based on information you received from the investigation, from the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. And also from what we could observe from the ground. You will see it later. Enables us to confirm -- I mean, say, that what is seen on this picture on this soccer field is groups of people, since the witnesses say these people were prisoners plus Bosnian Serb guards. This picture shows them at that date, that hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the next page. 44 in e-court. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a close-up picture of -- I mean, a zoom, in fact, of the same picture as previously, where you can -- this time it's marked by the provider also people on football field. So according to our knowledge, these people, as I just indicated, are prisoners, lying in rows, and also guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the provider wasn't there either. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The provider is an aerial platform and the provider is US government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But whether these were prisoners or not, the US platform wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We meanwhile receive the evidence so there is no problem with it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, again, let's clearly distinguish between what you can tell us, what we hear from witnesses and what you learned from witnesses, and to say that the provider told us that these are prisoners --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I said people. The witnesses -- there is a misunderstanding, I mis-expressed myself maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The witnesses say these people were prisoners. The picture says they are people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the Prosecution does consider that the evidence of -- the information on this aerial image from the provider is evidence and should have some weight. The weight you give it only up to you, of course. But you'll, of course, test it with all the witnesses. But it is more than just a label, in our view, because it's -- the provider has said that they stand by this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, we have heard testimony about these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. 45 in e-court. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same soccer field, a still photograph taken from -- I took from a helicopter. You can see the road. You can recognise the football field. And just after that, you enter Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you remind us where Milici is, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milici is -- if you continue this road, I would say maybe, I don't remind very well, maybe 3 kilometres we arrive in Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Direction south. This picture is oriented south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The picture is facing south. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next -- next page. E-court 46. What 's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a picture of this football field. I took it in April 1996. And the men on this football field are Bosnian Serb soldiers, dog handlers. The interest of it is to give an indication of the size of a man on this football field that you can then compare with the dots that you can see on the aerial imagery. To give an indication of the size of objects on the aerial imagery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next site, which you've got -- is marked as Konjevic Polje, and we see your blue dot near that. So let's go onto the next page. 48 in e-court. What is -- where is this and what is it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is at the -- very close to the intersection of Konjevic Polje but going towards the direction of Bratunac. The right of the picture is Bratunac. It is oriented north. It is another military facility in this area. It is the -- the 5th Engineer Battalion who is located at that place. One witness claims having surrendered at that spot and was initially taken to this -- to this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What's the circle?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The circle positions the -- the guard house that he describes as being the first point he was taken to when he exited -- when he went down the hill and exited the wooded area and arrived at this little -- at what he said was a guard house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: After reviewing or receiving this information from the witness, did you have a chance to go to this area on the ground and see if there was anything related to what he had said?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next picture. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the -- the military facility seen from the road. And the first thing you see at the left is, indeed, the guard house that he had described and that he recognised when we brought him back to this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture was taken before, but at a later stage we came back with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next -- next picture. 50. Where is this, and what's the significance of your markings?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, again, the intersection of Konjevic Polje facing the north. You have the Jadar river at the left of the picture. And at the right of the picture, where the blue line is, is the direction of Bratunac. The building circled in blue is a hangar. This witness says that after having spent a moment at the 5th Engineer Battalion he was taken to this house where prisoners were regrouped. And it's not a house, it's a hangar. It is the only picture we have of this hangar, since it was destroyed one year later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember what's there now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a gas station located on this -- on this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One year after you took this photograph, was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The following summer it was destroyed and then there was a -- I think during one year there was nothing and the gas station was already there in 1998. We wanted to probe a suspect site, looking for bodies, but it was a mission impossible without destroying the gas station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You mean that -- when did you take the photograph to the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This one was taken -- it's marked on it, it's 26 April 1997, this one, sorry. So it was destroyed in 1998. Yep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One year after this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- picture was taken --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was -- two things, sorry. Because there is another one. This -- the first one we should have shown, in fact, is this one because the other one has a more --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we're a little bit mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are we talking about which photograph, the one that's on e-court now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that is on e-court is April 1996. The previous one was 1997. It was destroyed in 1998 to construct the gas station. But we have these pictures that match what the witness told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. This one was taken in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one we have on the screen now is -- was taken 13 April 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the one with the blue --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one before -- the one after -- the one before, sorry, was taken 26 April 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But this area doesn't exist any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And since then it has been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As well as things changed a lot in the area. On previous picture, just as -- for an example, there is a church, an Orthodox church, this one was constructed that year, in 1997. It did not exist in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was surprised by the speed of construction because there's quite a bit of construction then apparently completed within one year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first thing that was constructed very quickly in the area were religious monuments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. We see now the close-up. I take it those are NATO vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were our escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's now go to the next regroupment site which you have noted in the table of contents as Sandici. And we see your blue mark by Sandici. So let's go to the next page. 53 in e-court. Where's this, what's the significance of the yellow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, did we see the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I had to skip it, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do we return on it? The map? Before this picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can if you have -- if you have something --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to spot the location but it is not necessary to return. We all know --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we're okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture is just to reference the location since we have a piece of footage from Mr. Zoran Petrovic in this area. On his footage, one can see at some point people surrendering, walking down a hill, and you have two reference points from this film, the pylon and also the open space where, on his film, one can see people arriving from. This is the road going towards the direction of Bratunac. Sandici is just after the curve and this hill where the pylon is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, to the left -- what -- which direction is this photograph facing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is taken from -- from west to east going towards Bratunac. Just before arriving to Sandici, coming from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Konjevic Polje is behind you --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- when you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you recall on the Petrovic film - we won't play it - but was there any firing of any weapons up at those hills at the time of the film, as you remember it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think we could hear on the film some shooting going on, which is quite logical, I would say. Yeah. It's mainly also where the -- the area where one of the Bosnian Serb soldiers who is interviewed says that they already had 5.000 people since the beginning of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this is in this spot, this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that with other witnesses. Let's go to the next page. 54 in e-court. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view from the -- the asphalt road. The photograph faces south. It is the -- the area from which the people who were on the hills started a massive surrender process on 13 July in the morning. They were coming down from these hills along the path that we can see on the -- on the right and arrived on this area, then had to cross the road that is just more or less where I took the picture from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I don't need to you go into detail, but did you learn that from a combination of things, or just witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- yeah, it's a combination of -- of things coming from the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the Petrovic video help you make these determinations as well?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The process is perfectly clear on the Petrovic video. This is the path that the people walk along. And on the Petrovic video you will see something of interest which is just the next picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- let's go to that picture then, the next one, and it's 55 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is photographed from the way the people are coming from, so now it's facing north, so it's the opposite. And the -- the men were walking just at the left of this white house, another white house, two-storey house just at the left. And you have a piece of footage of this surrender process on Zoran Petrovic happening right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question, on the previous picture we saw a small structure approximately 2 and a half metres high and to the right. Is that visible on this one? Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by any chance the structure we see at the right middle side of this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took the first picture from the left of the small structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From the left of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Left seen from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you are -- when I took the photograph, so the right on this -- on this picture. At the very right of this picture, just at the angle of the small structure is from where I took the previous picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see a corner. I see on the previous picture, I see a small white structure with what seems to be a door or an entry. Now is that visible or is that hidden at the back of what we see now on our screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the -- at the right, very right of this picture. I was standing next to the small, little, destroyed house that you can see at the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is why on the previous picture you could see a part of the wall of this small structure at the right of the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Were you standing from this point of view before the structure on the right-hand side of the structure or behind the structure --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- while you're taking the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the previous picture I was standing at the right of this photograph next to the small structure that you can see, and this little structure is indicated by no witness. We don't know if this was used for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, this is not my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Look at the screen. We see the small structure on the right-hand side of the picture. When you took the other photograph, were you standing behind or on the right-hand side of that building or in front of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The little structure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is why we can see part of the wall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's clear. But where next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seen on the photograph a little bit left, a little bit left and a little bit behind there so that this is why you can see this piece of wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're getting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would I see you -- if you would be standing there at that moment this picture was taken, would I be able to see you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or would you be hidden behind --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be just behind -- just behind the corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're getting to an aerial that might help. Could we go to the next -- the next page, 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask, I see a lot of small items in front of this white house. Could you tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is a Muslim graveyard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and all the abandoned things, all of the things you see on the ground are abandoned material from this surrender process. This picture was taken in early 1996 so everything was still on the ground at that moment. So you have a lot of plastics from HCR, a lot of personal items of little interest but among them also some of interest. We collected IDs, we collected documents with names on them, matched them with the missing list, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So if we could be at 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is an aerial picture of the area. On the following one there will be the markings, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... be easier with the markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the markings. The next page, then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you have one before with the yellow markings, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. There should be 57 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Same explanation than previously. But based on this aerial, going from the top of the picture, the dotted yellow line is the path followed by those who were surrendering. The two-storey white house is now pointed as the destroyed house. Just next to this house you would see on the Zoran Petrovic video prisoners surrendering, one being ordered to take off his T-shirt. This happens here. And when the people crossed the asphalt road were taken to a meadow where they were regrouped. The group of people the provider marked on the label is circled and designated group of prisoners. I did the marking. And shows the location of them. I also pointed the three destroyed houses, since these are features witnesses talk about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask if we had the opportunity to see the destroyed house in another picture which is on the left side of this aerial image? The single house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The little destroyed house we were talking for the previous pictures? Are you talking about this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We cannot see it because just at the left of the one that I marked with an arrow as destroyed house and this small structure is now under the arrow. It is just at the left of this two-storage house. But this small structure, no one talks about it so I never used it as any kind of reference point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In yellow you described this house as destroyed house. Is that the white house we have seen in the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the big one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The big one, the white --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the two-storage one, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You called it the white house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Absolutely, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can go to the next aerial which gives a bit of a better picture of it. It's 58 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this a blow-up in fact of the previous one. Since it indicated group of people, you now know where they are, since they were circled on the previous picture. And you can also see the asphalt road and also the two-storage white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about the now infamous little house? Do you see where that is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture is very blurry because it is getting closer. It's at the left -- maybe ... yeah. At the left, you have a big tree and in fact the big tree is hiding the little structure. But it's just at the left at the angle of the big tree. Since the picture is taken during summer, there are leaves on the tree. And on the other picture showing the grave and the two-storage house, you have the tree but without leaves. This is why you also perfectly see the little structure. And it's not taken from the air, so it's not hidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And as we look at this photograph, were there witnesses that were actually on this meadow that provided statements to you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that consistent with this conclusion that this is people on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one. 59.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one further question. Could you indicate where now the graveyard on this picture is in relation to the house. Is it up or is it down, on the picture, of course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we are looking now at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards the south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are now looking towards the south. Yes. So we're looking at the facade of the building which is not visible on the big picture we saw before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is clear to me. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we can go to 59, the next photograph. What is -- what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this picture was taken in 1997. But, as I told you, in 1996, we searched the area, and on this area, we found a lot of abandoned items, stretchers, ID cards, documents. And if you take the picture of the left, it's very difficult to make any assessment of numbers because the photograph is taken with an angle and people are sitting on a slope so it's very hard to assess. But the rough location that I narrowed down on purpose, not to make it larger but smaller, is, in my opinion, the reference on the ground is now marked with the yellow -- the yellow line which is the -- the location of this group of people that we could see on the previous photograph. This is now seen from the ground. The following year it was a corn field, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now let's go to the next one. 60. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same view than the previous one indicating the precise location of an event that can be seen in the Zoran Petrovic video where, indeed, a group of people we believe are prisoners were sitting. And at the moment of this film when it stops, this group of people are sitting precisely where I boxed the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So the -- the picture up in the left-hand corner, where is that from? That still picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the video taken on the spot by Zoran Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back now briefly to the trial video, exhibit 65 ter 28780, from 19:23 to 20:12, V000-9267.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know or recall who that is at 19:42:5?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The man that is called Boro is Colonel Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And this -- okay. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So now it's moving towards the group of people that we could see on -- and now it's closing up on something that is going to happen but then he is cutting his film.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So is this the shot you have up in -- on your photo book?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And that's at 19:58:8. And -- all right. That's just a -- we've slo-mo'd it so that it can be viewed in slow motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, your chapters change from regroupment to execution area, south. And that is -- let's go to page 61 in e-court. And we -- we see the blue dot at the far left at Luke school. And then we see a red dot in Vlasenica, above Vlasenica. Can you tell us the significance of these? Are these related?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The witness who claims having taken to Luke school after having been separated prior -- attempting to cross at Kladanj said he was taken on board of a little truck. He arrived at what he -- he describes due to lamps at the side of the street as being the entrance of Vlasenica. Vlasenica was the HQ of the Drina Corps. This truck turned left and after a while of drive, bumpy drive, he claimed having escaped at a location where there were already dead bodies. We attempted to find this place. We even then brought him back to the location, and it was a mission impossible to find any evidence of -- of execution or dead bodies in this place. And we could not also find aerial imagery that could assist us orient ourselves in this area which is very hard to investigate in because everything looks a bit similar. Little hills, soft hills, little valleys, impossible to -- to find without additional indication. So, as I said, the missions were aimed to confirm or not. On this case, we could not confirm the final stage of the story of this witness by hard evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So the red dot, is that meant to be any particular location?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a particular location. It's really an estimate of where this could be. It's just north of Vlasenica. No additional info.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue on to the next site which is labelled in your contents as "Cerska," and we see a red dot sort of between Cerska and -- and the roads. Can you tell us about this? Briefly.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The big hill I was referring to at one point is just underneath, you know, Konjevic Polje, north of Nova Kasaba, and from this hill witnesses were looking to find a way to -- to cross this area and, in that process, observed a certain number of things, including for one of them, he saw three buses entering the direction of the Cerska valley. These buses were followed by an APC and -- an armoured personnel carrier, and also a short time after that by an excavator. And once out of sight, he could hear at some point intensive shooting coming from this valley. Then the buses are leaving the area. So there was an assumption of something happening in that place that we tried to find using additional witnesses who didn't see what happened but one walked on this -- on this path leading to the valley of Cerska at one point stepped in a pool of blood. He was barefoot. But we finally could have additional info by a group of other people who had escaped, hid themselves at the -- at the end of this valley of Cerska, and on their way back, because they didn't know how to -- how to leave, they decided to return towards -- towards the Srebrenica area and at one point smelled a very bad smell. And since we had filmed the entire way of this valley from -- in all these directions by film, they could indicate as some reference point from where then we could find the location, because we made two missions there. The first mission was unsuccessful, but the second one was.
