utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next -- bearing in mind the map that we see now and the location you're talking about, let's go to the next one. Page 63, here. And we see this -- what looks like a main road and your arrow. Can you orient us again? Where is this main road going to, where's the arrow going to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The picture faces north. The big hill is out of the picture, out of the frame at the right. The asphalt road at the bottom goes towards Nova Kasaba. At the top, Konjevic Polje, and then either Bratunac, either Zvornik. So the initial witness was out of this picture to the right. The big hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the black arrow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The black arrow is the path to enter the valley of Cerska, which is in between the two hills we see at the left of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photograph, 64. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is facing west. So now we can see the hill we always talk about, the observation point, the observation hill. And the dirt road leading to the entrance of the valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is taken shortly before entering the valley. And after the point where the first Humvee is seen on the picture, then you enter woods and you are out of sight of the hill, which is also something that the witness said, that at one point he couldn't see them anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just try to compare the previous one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering whether -- and even the one before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 64. The one -- it would be 64 in e-court. There we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now that road that we see in the picture going from top to bottom and then turning to the left of the picture, is that the beginning of the black arrow in the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- previous page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is the black arrow, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the first thick part of this line ending in a thinner line with the black arrow, the first part, that is what we see -- and I'm just trying to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, where the Humvee is and the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the bridge is then approximately where the thick line --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is ending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is ending and where the thin line is starting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we see that the river on the -- both on the previous and on this one is more or less visible because of the bushes on both sides --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the river. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we are now -- we should be. We've gone up that road and now we're on 66 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this -- this picture is the suspect area we ended up finding. Here, it is looking towards the entrance of the valley. This is approximately, maybe 1 -- 1 -- let's -- not more than 2 kilometres inside the valley. But we are now on this picture facing the entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that approximately where we saw the black arrow previously? The point of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, no. It is further inside the valley. It is -- it is roughly where I did put the red dot on the picture of page 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, already a bit into the valley --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next picture then. 67 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another view of the same -- the same spot but looking in the opposite direction. The vehicles are pointing their front towards the entrance, but the picture is facing the direction of the end of the Cerska valley, so it's ... so it is west.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- still a little bit on this one, because we will see it from other angles, where the colleague in blue is standing is an area we will describe later as being the line of execution. And at the right of the vehicles, you can see disturbed soil that we will mention later on other pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm confused now. You say the end of the valley. That means west. Now I see the picture with the vehicles. If the vehicles are heading for the end of the valley, then the picture is facing east.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The front of the vehicles are facing the entrance and the back of the vehicles are facing the end of the valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I understand. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue to the next -- the next picture. 68. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also now seen from another angle, since on the previous one it was not possible to see, but it is a steep slope that is at the edge of this road. It was not visible on the previous one. It looked like flat, but in reality it is quite a steep slope. That in fact we will see it contains the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next picture then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who are these folks? What are you doing?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So these are the colleagues I was with for this mission. And, here, we are probing this area. It was a preliminary mission in order to find out if there was a future need for any exhumation of that spot. And here we are probing the area. We did a three, three probes, three holes in order to check what was under this soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we go to the next photo. 70. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a result of the first probe, we discovered human remains that are visible at the bottom of the picture. One can clearly see a leg and a shoe on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to the next photo. 71.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the result of the second probe, the second hole. And, here, you can see a skull with some hair attached on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the hole that we see?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hole we see, I would not be able to say anything about it because the probes, we start them by what we call -- we call pick and sniff. That means take an iron stick, you push it in the soil to probe, and then you take it out and you smell. Depending on the smell, you start or not dig. So I cannot exclude that this hole is for sure not maybe a bullet-hole but just a result of the probe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next photo. 72.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the -- the finding of the third hole that we dug, which is a body in a civilian jacket. And at the left is the skull.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's now go to 74. Sorry, 74 is the next one. Next page in e-court. And we see another United States aerial image from the graphics. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a picture we requested after. Since we had found the place, we wanted to know if we could have an indication of date of creation of this crime scene. You can see, first the picture dated the 5th July. This is the path going toward the valley, going -- at the end of the Cerska valley and the area that we probed. On 27 July, one can see disturbed soil, disturbed earth. I circled the area, and with two boxes, one being in fact the location of the grave, and the -- the box at the right is disturbed soil from the -- the hill at the opposite side of the path. We will provide more pictures of this from the ground. But it indicates that at July 5th there was nothing there. And on 27, the site is there. So the only conclusion is that it is between the 5th and the 27th. We do not have -- I mean, at that time, we did not have a -- I mean, at that time we did not have aside the witness testimony and we had the feeling it was the 13. We had no precise indication aside that. I heard that since then there is more precise information to precisely date this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And these pictures are north/south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These pictures are west oriented -- the top of the picture is more or less the west. It's the end of the Cerska valley, going towards the end of the Cerska valley .

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page. 75 in e-court?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So here is the -- the situation seen from the ground. Vehicles pointing the front towards the entrance of the valley. At the right of the picture is the -- the location of the grave. So obviously where the yellow markers are was the line where the people were made to -- to stand, shot, and fall along the steep hill. At the left of the picture, the excavator that was seen by the witness took the soil and then covered the bodies, simply covered them with this soil. This is pointed by the big yellow arrow. And the two colleagues at the left at this moment are collecting shell casings. I couldn't recall exactly how many we collected that day. It was a preliminary mission, but this is where the firing line was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, if you say "facing the entrance of the valley," we are in the valley now. That would mean facing east, is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And these yellow things on the ground, we see a 7 and a 6, what is that for?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They mark the -- what at that moment is the estimate of the size of the grave, so in fact the line on which the execution took place. It's a rough estimate at that moment. But I would refer to -- later on to a full exhumation report because this place was fully exhumed the following year, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have witnesses for that. Though, do you recall how many bodies were found here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 150. Which was our estimate, because we roughly counted 50 per bus, three buses, so we thought probably 150, and I think this is more or less very precisely the final number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How are we doing for time? I can't see the watch --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are at one hour from when we resumed. So that would be -- if this would be an appropriate moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we'll take a break. And we'll resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, again, I use the time to deal with MFI D189. D189 was MFI'd during the testimony of Anthony Banbury, 7th of February of this year, pending provision of the Defence of the B/C/S translation. The Chamber has been informed by the Defence that the B/C/S translation of Exhibit D189 has been uploaded in e-court under doc ID 1D03-1002. The Chamber requests the Registry to attach this B/C/S translation to the original and -- unless there would be any objections by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the person who is reviewing this is unfortunately out for the remainder of this week. Could I suggest that the Chamber go ahead with this, and if there's any problem with the translation, we'll bring it to the attention of the Chamber on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then D189 is admitted into evidence. And we expect the Prosecution to re-visit the matter, well, let's say, within two weeks if there would be any problem as far as this translation is concerned so that we could reconsider it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Ruez. Mr. McCloskey will continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to finish up Cerska, can you confirm that there -- there was no survivor of this execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of our knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And there -- there was no witness, to your knowledge, of anyone that witnessed the actual execution?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one at my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the next site, Nova Kasaba, which I don't -- it's 76, the next e-court page. And you've noted that in red there as we're now getting very familiar with these villages. Can we go to the next page. 77. And if you could briefly tell us what these boxes are.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The orientation here is the top right is going towards Nova Kasaba. The bottom left towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ruez. I just want to interrupt. The -- unless asked, I don't want to you explain about the red box because I don't believe the Judges will be hearing any evidence about that. So if you could -- the two big boxes, just concentrate on that unless asked.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two boxes show area of undisturbed soil. The two black ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then let's go to the next photo. That first one was dated 13 July. Now we see this one on this page, 78, dated 27 July. And -- and the big boxes, what does that indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the -- the same areas of undisturbed soil photographed 13 July and on 27 July. One can see that there are obvious traces of disturbance at these locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And let's go to the next page. Tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photographs at the top show how the ground looks like. And the yellow circles indicate locations that we can see one on the aerial imagery and the other one seen from the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you remind us, we see this road that we are probably getting familiar with. On -- which way -- which town is in the direction right, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But since the two pictures are taken from a different direction, on the bottom, the bottom black and white picture, the aerial, bottom right is the direction of Nova Kasaba. The left is the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the top, the coloured picture, the right is the direction of Konjevic Polje; the left, the direction of Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have a chance to probe this disturbed soil we can see in this aerial image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did that in 1996, in June 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to page 80, the next page. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the result of the probe that we did that day. We opened -- we opened this -- this site and found what we believed was a first layer of bodies. On this picture, in fact, it's a [indiscernible] of bodies but there are six bodies on this picture. The aim was, as usual, to find multiple remains, since we cannot spark any exhumation if there are not multiple remains. If there would be only one, it would be of no -- no real interest. So this one was the preliminary check before any further exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'd --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right, it's me; and on the left, it's another colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you -- let's go to the next photo. I believe you took close-ups of this picture. So that's 81 in e-court. Is this a close-up of one of the people who was next to you in the grave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the previous picture, he is the one who is close to my boots. And here we can see the back of a man with his arms -- I mean, wearing a civilian shirt with green stripes, and he has ligatures at his wrists. The hands are tied in his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's the yellow arrow?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the yellow arrow, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. The next picture.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another close shot of another body found in this location. At the left, can you see his head. Then civilian jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. The civilian jacket, as you tell us, seems to be -- well, pretty clean, which surprises slightly. Was there any manipulation before this photograph was taken, or was it cleaned or was it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We cleaned these bodies by hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm mainly talking about the jacket at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The jacket, same thing. We took the soil that was on top of it, we took it away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But has it been removed, cleaned, and then replaced or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. Not at all. No, no. We just opened this first layer. Then refilled the hole as it was, waiting for the full exhumation to take place. We didn't remove any item. We just cleaned the soil on the surface, cleaned the soil off the bodies. The jacket was not taken off this man at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you wipe it off --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the dust and the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And would that be the same process you did at Cerska, so you just exposed the bodies, photographed them, and then covered them up for later exhumation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go -- well, we are at the next page.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was this the same body? We see a bit of the blue jacket that we just saw.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same one. What you see at the bottom right is a head of another body which is underneath the body we saw. The interest of this one is that -- it was visible on the previous picture but this one has the hands attached in his back as well with -- with an iron -- not iron. I mean, a metal, a metal rope which is very flexible metal and that you can easily use to fix things but also attach people. This type of metal is quite common in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So which yellow arrow is pointing at this -- what we would call a wire?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the wire is the left arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the right arrow points to the wedding ring of this man. It is his finger, his fingers and a wedding ring.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's go to another of the sites that were thought to be or reported to be possible execution sites, the Jadar river which we now -- is that site marked in red here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photo -- yes, this is the location, the rough -- I mean, the location of this next site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And so if we just visualise that, that's that road north going towards Zvornik that we've seen before. So let's now go to 85. Another photograph we've seen before but we now have this red arrow. What is that about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, first of all, the blue box points where the hangar in which the -- the witness claims having been kept prior being put on board of the bus. It happened at random that that day there was a bus just next to this hangar but picture date was 1997. And the red arrows points the direction towards which this bus would lead this group of 16 prisoners, and it points to the entrance of -- it's a kind of canyon, in fact. It's very, very narrow access to the Drina River that then leads towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photo for that. What does this tell us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a view of what I just said, narrow valley. The -- it is pointing direction south here, so this is the direction from where the bus came, then drove along this -- the road going towards Zvornik in between these two steep hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the arrow is -- what direction is the red arrow pointing?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's pointing towards Zvornik and towards the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you describe to us those two lines we see underneath the red line? It looks --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first one is the asphalt road and the shiny line is the Jadar river.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The first one means that one next to the red arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And so -- so I take it by this -- had -- have we hit the spot yet that you were looking for on -- or we must continue up the canyon towards Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to continue a bit. [Indiscernible] bus-stop location that we are going to hit first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next photo.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is just before arriving at the spot the prisoners were unloaded. It's again to show what type of landscape it is and also remote place. It's a remote place. It is quite well hidden, one can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do we see the cars driving on the road which is indicated on the previous picture by the dotted red line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, and the vehicles are driving like the bus would do it that day, towards the north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in the direction of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, like the last sites you've described, are you looking for the site described by a particular witness?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Since it was in no way possible for us alone to find the location, we had to bring the witness in the area. We did this, we couldn't do it before. I think we did it 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's -- let's go to the next -- the next shot, which is 88. Here we see a -- from the air, a tire of some sort?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. It's the tire of a Black Hawk helicopter. It's a picture taken from the air. It shows the location where we stopped and which is the so-called bus-stop. It's an area where in -- because of the narrow road, it is an area where a bus can easily stop. It is where the witness told us he was unloaded from the bus and walked towards the river, which is the -- the arrow that I added to the picture is the access path to what he claims being -- the execution spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could we ask, in which direction is going to the right top. Is that north? And to the left, further down, is that to the south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Top right is towards Zvornik. And the left towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Can we go to the next photograph. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area where the witness brought us to, that he recognised as being the -- the spot where he was made to stand facing the river and among -- with the 16 others was shot. We were at this moment trying to find shell casings in this location. The -- we can only see the witness -- we can see his trousers. Here, the man with black trousers. And we are at this moment looking for shell casings there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you find any?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We couldn't implement the story of this witness. We couldn't find any body. We couldn't find shell casings. But the following picture might provide a possible explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 90.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- this witness claims that once he was shot, he -- he fell in the water and succeeded to float on the river. Crossed the opposite side and then gave other reference points that we found. The thing is that since we did this search in 1998, we do not know how this river flows, really, during spring, summer, winter time. And, as you can see here, it seems that it happens that the water is quite high. You can see these logs on the -- on the other bank of the river. We had additional photographs with items hanging at quite a height above the level of the water, so one could assume that the river washed away shell casings. Maybe even bodies, if they were not collected. It is very difficult to collect in such a place. I would not believe that anyone went to collect the bodies here, but no one can say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you give us one example of -- of what you're able to confirm from his -- his account after he was shot? Any locations, anything?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He says that, on the opposite side, there was a military structure, and, indeed, very close by this place was the location of the compound of the so-called Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you -- did you find that yourselves -- yourself?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I mean, with the assistance of the intelligence we could collect in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether or not you saw the -- a bullet-hole in his back, or a photograph of it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, indeed. I mean, he provided his medical -- medical information. I won't say the name, but he even provides the name of the police personnel who shot him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go onto the next one, which you've labelled the Kravica warehouse. And there will be other numerous witnesses on this so we do want to get through the basics of this, Mr. Ruez, to save a little time. Let's start. We see the blue and red. Can you briefly describe the blue and the red, how they relate to each other, Sandici?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The blue is the rough position of the meadow of Sandici we showed previously, and the right spot is the also approximate location of the Kravica warehouse. The next photograph will show that the distance is very -- a short distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to that. 93. And orient us with this, could you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. The picture is facing the direction towards Bratunac. I am -- I take -- I took this picture at the left of this two-storage building and the little structure we talked about. So it's a clear view towards the warehouse. The Sandici meadow is at the left of the picture out of frame, it's in my back at the left, and the dotted arrow points to the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next shot. And, again, orient us which direction is Bratunac and which is Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Top left of the picture is direction Bratunac. And, here, it's a helicopter view. Just at the bottom left of the picture but also just -- in fact, just at the limit of the picture is the meadow, the Sandici meadow. But this gives you a clear indication of the distance, since one group -- I mean, one survivor says he was taken on board of the bus and then another group was taken by foot. This is the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot. 95. Again, which -- which way is Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue arrow points the direction of Bratunac. So the people were coming from the right where the Sandici meadow is. Only one -- one building of this warehouse complex was used for this event. It's the one that is along the side of the road, and it is marked with the red box.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you -- are you getting your information about this warehouse from two survivors?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, yes. Two survivors. One from the east part and one from the west part. The west being the left picture and the east, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry. It's the opposite. Because we are facing south here. Mm-hm. We are not facing the north. We are facing south. So Bratunac is at the left, east.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There will be a test on these geographic locations afterward, but we have that ready for you later. All right. Let's go to the next photograph. 96. The snow is back.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But to get pictures at a date as close as possible to the events, this is a stop that we made during the so-called Shattuck mission at the end of January 1996. We made a stop at the warehouse in order to take some photographs and use the opportunity also to scratch a sample of what we found on the walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's see the next page. We can see what that meant. And what is this? It seems the other side of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The photographs of January, it's to match with the aerials so that we can determine, you know, the story about the east part and the story about the west part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this tied in to the location of the two victims you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the information on this place is -- everything is coming from these two survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page. 93. And we see -- again, it looks look that nice green aerial from perhaps your helicopter?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, absolutely. And it is to show by comparing it with the black and white aerial photographs that were the better -- better version of how it looks, really, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So that's another US aerial image dated 13 July. And you have circled in yellow what?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In yellow, I circled two buses. The -- the witness who claims having survived an execution on this east part said he was taken there by bus. And apparently one bus after that stayed blocked on the spot because of a flat tire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot. This appears to be a similar shot --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So now we are going to deal with the west part. So this survivor in the west part was marched there within a large group. They arrived at this warehouse and entered through a small -- a small door, which is most certainly the door which is at the -- at the left of the squared box.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think you can mark on this -- just -- I'm not sure -- there's a lot of potential doors. Could you mark the door you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to mark the one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, or clearly explain which door you're referring to. That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On the square box there is one big hole which was made by a bulldozer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- before we start marking, if the witness can explain to us to which he -- to what he refers, then -- is it the opening at the right-hand side --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it should be the one at the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the left which is composed of three separate or even four separate -- or is it the small, the lower one. Yes. It's marked now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has been marked. Then I take it that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sign it? I have to put my initials on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not necessarily. But we have to separate it and -- Now may I take it that we do not want the whole of the book --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- attached to this marking. Madam Registrar, is there any way to separate this page as marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we can save it separately as a marked photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And that would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P1129, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless there's any need for any other markings on this one, Mr. McCloskey, P -- and let me now make no mistake. P1129 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What would be the 65 ter number of this P or -- or the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar has separated it so there's no 65 ter number yet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As the same number the -- as the saved picture, they receive IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They receive IC numbers. Mr. McCloskey, I was informed when you referred to page 93 on page 66, line 8, you apparently wanted to refer to -- I don't know whether you did it or whether it was someone else's slight error, but it's 98 from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I take your word for that, of course. And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's to avoid that others -- let me -- I'll check in e-court immediately. That's ... let me see. 93, 98. What we have on our screen now. Let me just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On the record it says: "Let's go to the next page, 93."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what we have now on our screen is -- it seems to be page 99 in e-court out of 274. That's what we see on our screen now. And that is also the separate page which was marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I -- I think I read the 8 as a 3, and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps. And then, finally, it turned out that it should be 99. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now we were -- you were talking about the account of the victim. The door he said. You identified the door that you thought may have been the door he went into, and did you go inside and see if you could determine anything inside that matched his story or resembled his story?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what were you looking for in there when you went inside the warehouse to -- what was his basic -- very briefly, his story that you were seeing if you could find?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Due to his account of events, we were looking mainly for bullet-holes, explosive traces, and blood and what was human features that could be found in it. During the very first visit, the only thing that I could do was scratch suspect -- suspect trace from the wall which appeared to be human, and then we returned during several missions to take more samples of all these elements. And there was then a full -- a full forensic examination done of this place. There is a full report on what was found in this location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. McCloskey, sorry to deal with the matter again. When you said, page 66, line 8, "93," you should have said "98." Then page 66, line 20, you said, "Let's go to the next shot," that then is page 99 in e-court. And it is page 99 which was separated and marked and was separately admitted. Where I said 98 should be 99, we had already moved to the next page. That -- should that be -- I would like to make life easier for anyone who comes after us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. This sequence is critical as -- of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So let's go into the warehouse. The next page, e-court 100.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a photograph from the inside of this west part of the warehouse. One can see quite a number of bullet-holes in -- in the walls. And the traces, you can see the rubbed traces and various reddish material there appeared to be tested as human blood. Also human hair and things like skin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next one. 101.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, so it's the -- another -- another area of the warehouse with black traces that happened to -- being explosive residues. And again, a certain number of human features glued on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now let's go to 102.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask what does the number 9 in the previous photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh. Yes, on -- on the -- there are indeed labels on this wall. We had with us a crime scene technician named John Gerns who took samples and labelled them according to his own way of doing. This sampling was also a kind of a preliminary step in case we would not be able to return to this area or that the place would be destroyed, so each time we did as much as we could during a very short period of time in the area. It was always go in, go out. We couldn't spend time on these places for security reasons also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But what does the number 9 indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took a sample at that location and labelled it 9. But I don't have his report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just follow up. Does that explain the 11 on the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then on this picture, in small figures, you also have 1, 2 and 3, or what looks like minus 1, minus 2, minus 3, and then minus something that I can't see. What do those indicate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the labelling that John Gerns did of his samples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go now to the next page. 102. Where does this fit into anything?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- the survivor claims that once he entered the warehouse, shots were -- bursts of fire were coming from the -- the open windows and grenades were thrown inside. We tried to check this part of his story during a search of the surroundings of the warehouse, found elements including a live grenade that was obviously forgotten there. It was just in front of the warehouse close to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I hope that's not in the evidence locker.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not. It was handed over for destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. The next page. 103.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is one of grenade handles that we found at the back of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is what is left over once the grenade is thrown. This piece of metal stays there at the location it has been thrown. It is something left behind of the grenade, hand-grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 104. Do you have any idea what this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought we would take them out but since they are here, it's no certainty but he -- the witness said also that RPGs were fired from the outside to inside. This could be - I just say "could be" - a hole made by an anti-tank rocket. The next picture shows it a bit better with the direction of possible firing from the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 105, then, please, next. Is this from the inside or outside?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is from the outside at the back of the warehouse. The window is facing the direction of the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. 106.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The survivor of the west part of the warehouse claimed that once he entered the -- the warehouse, he -- people were compressed inside, and the reason why he managed to survive is that he crawled into a little structure inside the warehouse that he calls the -- a guard house. It's a -- it was a -- a room inside this location. The first time we went there, the first mission, in January, there was nothing like this inside, so it was a problem because no explanation how he could have survived with all this. But, in fact, returning there in April, the next picture will show that just at the -- at the entrance, indeed, once inside, there was -- there was something there that had been destroyed in -- probably in the process of taking the bodies out with heavy equipment and the traces of it are extremely obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- I'll go to that. But what's this yellow arrow on the current photo?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow marks the direction of entering and the location where this little structure was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. 107.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is what -- I believe is what is left of so-called guard house inside. One can see that at the bottom there was a room here with a -- a blue -- the blue tiles at the bottom and the points where this structure was attached to the wall. It obviously has been completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 108. Where is this and what -- what is it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There -- there was a little pile of rubbish at the -- at one of the sides of this warehouse. We went through a manual search of this rubbish, and this is what we could -- we could find. There are shell casings, a piece of licna karta, certain number of human bones. They were assessed as being human by Professor Bill Haglund. And a few items, including fake teeth, that was left behind by those who cleaned the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 109.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So after -- after the execution at the west part took place the execution at the east part, according to the person who survived this part, who heard the noises of the first row of killings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you could just -- I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. McCloskey. If we just go back to previous picture with collections of shell casings. There are things that look like books there. Are you able to tell us what they are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's the cover page of a licna karta. Licna karta is the ID card. But there were no names in -- in these. It's only the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The cover.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the cover.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So 109 was identifying the -- the other side of the warehouse for the next survivor who you've just explained his account briefly. And let's go to 110. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a photograph of this east part taken from the entrance. So this is supposed to be the area where the people were stored, sitting -- sitting with this wall in their back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- one can see traces of bullets fired against this wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. 111. You've got a yellow arrow you've marked?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, during the process of this warehouse by the forensic experts, they processed only one part of the warehouse and forgot the other part. So, at one point, I passed again by this warehouse and scratched a sample marked with the yellow arrow which is a -- looks like a blood-stain, and this was analysed by the Dutch forensic lab as being human blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 112. Is this related to the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a close-up of this blood-stain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 113. We're still at that site of the warehouse. We see you put a yellow arrow.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. The -- the witness says that he climbed to jump out of the window at the back of the warehouse, the first window, and the arrow points to the window that he is supposed having jumped through.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 114. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the back of this warehouse. The first window when you go towards the left is the window from where he says having jumped. He -- there was a corn field at that time, and, indeed, behind the warehouse what you can see, the little sticks, it's leftover of corn. Now, it's a view of the location he says having escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To be clear, if we start from the right side of the photo we're looking at and move towards the left, is -- is it that first --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- one we come to?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one going from left to right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: With a white reflection of some sort in it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of snow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's go to the next one. 115.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a view of the front of the warehouse. No -- no specific claim of survivors for this one. But in order to show that this man was probably not the only one who tried to survive by escaping, jumping windows, I could find an element that assists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what are you --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What are focussing on in this picture?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this one, I would mark it with the pen, there is a shoe trace --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That sort of complicates things --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Just underneath the window that is in the middle of the picture, above the first bullet-hole underneath is a shoe trace. We have a close-up on the next picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next picture. 116.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's a shoe trace, but it's a reverse shoe. It's not the shoe of someone who is climbing; it is of a shoe of someone who is getting out. Interest of it is again to show that this witness is -- might not be the only one who tried to escape by jumping out through the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So is the window we saw in the previous photo right above this -- the shoe print?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's go to 117. We see Studio B again. So I take it this is a Petrovic -- what is -- what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a still from a few seconds of footage filmed by Zoran Petrovic who arrived on that spot on July 13 together with Colonel Borovcanin. These are part of the, in brackets, lost pictures that were found later. And it shows -- the main -- the main entrance, the one that was then partially destroyed by a bulldozer who entered the warehouse to pick out -- take out the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where do you get that account from that a bulldozer came to take out bodies?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the witness who survived in this location and stayed there during several hours prior escaping by night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what do you use this photo for in your -- in your book analysis? If we go -- the previous -- excuse me, the next line of photos, you have a particular purpose for this, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was mainly relevant for the trial of Colonel Borovcanin. It's much less, to be honest, here. The question was, was this execution finished or was it still ongoing. According to analysis made on these walls, I tend to believe that it was ongoing since they are -- after this shot, this picture, there are additional bullet-holes to be found on the walls, so one could think that someone later on fired on this wall. This is not the case. It would mean that there were still shots fired after this piece of footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's briefly go back to the trial video, exhibit 65 ter 28780, from 35:00 to 36:55, V000-9267, to play this -- this clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've ended that clip at 36:55:6. Is that slow motion clip where you took your still from, if we could go back to 117 in e-court of your book. So we -- we see this. Is this the Kravica warehouse you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is that basically a still of the -- of what we just saw, the drive-by of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you remind us what direction is the car driving in as it's driving by? We can see this pictures pass.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So from the right to the left, so going back to the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now let's go through these next shots briefly. Let's go to 118. And if you could just explain what this was about.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to show that the -- this door again was broken by some heavy equipment. One year later, they started reconstructing a part of it, but these markings in blue, I'm not the one who put them on it. They don't fit with the demo. Again, we could -- if you want, in a bit of time, go to bullet-hole if there is still a need for this demonstration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, I think we should just go through this --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't go through the blue ones. I didn't put them and I don't agree with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Don't know where they came from. So let's go to the next page. 119.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in red is the missing part. The missing part is -- is bigger than what one could think just by looking at the picture at the bottom. And depending on the angle as well as -- the height, as well as the -- the -- how large it is, looks also a bit different. The references are the yellow markings with the round circles that put in relation the situation after and before the destruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of interest it's to show the height of the way the openings were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, here, you have what I believe was the -- the way the situation was looking at the time, what it was -- the size of this opening. At the bottom of the picture, at the bottom right, you can see one bar next to the door. That's -- from top to -- bottom from top, the bar next to the right of the frame. And on the picture, the big one, I had to re-put this bar with the computer to show where it was. So it shows again what were the missing parts of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to 122.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. So, here, it puts the -- puts the two pictures in relation. It is more or less the same but still at the bottom right is not exactly, I think, the one we saw before. It's another angle. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 123.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So at the moment of the events when Zoran Petrovic filmed the place, at the top, on the right, there are -- there is a marking with bullet-holes and also at the left of the picture in the red box are locations of -- of impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And -- and to be clear, the top photograph is from the Petrovic film.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one at the top which has the logo Studio B is the one from the Zoran Petrovic film.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: From 13 July?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from 13 July. And the bottom one is taken in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what does this comparison tell us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next picture should show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 124.

utterances.text: In fact, this picture is -- was given to me by an American officer. I think they use it for their own purposes, and we rephotographed. I think it was a poster-size document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page. And this you've labelled Grbavci and gym. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]

utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, any objection if I would read a decision on the admission of the report of Mr. Van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, the accused is not present at this moment. Then I will deliver that decision, which is a decision on the admission of the report of Witness Patrick van der Weijden. By notice of the 19th of November, 2012, the Prosecution served Witness Van der Weijden's report on the Defence. By notice of the 19th of December, 2012, the Defence objected to its admission. In a decision of the 9th of January, 2013, the Chamber, inter alia, deferred its decision on the admission of the report until the time of Witness Van der Weijden's testimony. Witness Van der Weijden testified before the Chamber on the 10th and the 11th of January of this year. Following the conclusion of the witness's testimony, the Defence and the Prosecution made supplementary oral submissions regarding the admission of the report. The Defence submits that the methodology used in preparing the report is not transparent in that, first, the witness has not identified with sufficient particularity all of the source material upon which he relied, and, second, the witness relied on sources obtained from the Internet and military manuals which were not identified in the report and were not made available to the Defence. In response, the Prosecution submits that the report contains adequate references to the source material. Further, the Prosecution suggests that any issues as regards references to source material go to the weight to be afforded to, and not the admissibility of, the report. In relation to sources which the witness could not fully identify when asked about them during his testimony, the Prosecution contends that these related to Unscheduled Incidents only. In relation to the use of Internet sources and military handbooks, the Prosecution submits that these sources form but a part of the witness's knowledge and are, in effect, subsidiary to his substantial experience as a sniper and sniping instructor. The Chamber considers that the report contains adequate references to written source material. The witness also testified that some of the material - for example, regarding the weaponry available to the VRS - was based on his personal observations at VRS check-points during his time with DutchBat in the former Yugoslavia. The Chamber considers that in referring to sources from the Internet and military manuals, the witness was explaining the basis for part of his knowledge, in addition to the knowledge he had accumulated from his direct experience as a sniper and sniping instructor. The Chamber considers that, on the whole, the report meets the minimum standards of reliability as required under Rule 89(C) and 94 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The report is therefore admitted into evidence. The Chamber underlines that the admission of the report is distinct from its evidential weight which the Chamber will determine in due course when assessing the totality of the evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. Then, since we may still have some time I will read another oral decision. The Chamber will deliver its decision on the Prosecution's urgent motion to add five documents to its Rule 65 ter exhibit list to tender through Witness RM048 and Witness RM013. On the 14th of February of this year, the Prosecution filed an urgent motion to add five documents to its Rule 65 ter exhibit list to tender through Witness RM048 and Witness RM013. On the 18th of February, the Prosecution put on the record that it no longer wished to tender four of the documents through RM048 but retained its request to add them to the Rule 65 ter exhibit list along with the fifth remaining document to be added to the list and to be tendered through Witness RM013. In court on the 19th of February, 2013, the Chamber granted the addition of the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 28736 to the Rule 65 ter exhibit list and the request to tender it through Witness RM013, who was scheduled to testify within a matter of days. Thus, the Chamber will now decide on the addition of the four remaining documents to the Rule 65 ter exhibit list. The Defence maintains its original objections on the ground of lack of good cause, as filed in their response on the 15th of February, 2013. The Chamber considers that the Prosecution has not shown good cause for the late addition of documents to its Rule 65 ter exhibit list. However, the Chamber finds that the four remaining documents are, prima facie, probative and of -- and relevant to incidents in Foca during the indictment period. The Chamber also considers that the documents are short in length and are no longer sought to be tendered through a witness due to testify in the immediate future. The Chamber therefore finds that the accused will not be unduly prejudiced by their addition to the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter exhibit list, and finds it to be in the interests of justice to allow the addition of the documents bearing provisional Rule 65 ter numbers 28732 up to and including 28735 to the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter exhibit list. And this concludes the Chamber's decision.

utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, if you are ready, please proceed.

utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We left off at the Grbavci school where you had just compared your actual observations to the account of the survivors and showed us -- what had matched up. utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]

The arrows at the -- at the right pin-point two -- two initially suspect sites that we now consider as being execution sites. After a few -- a short drive, the road became bumpy and then the trucks stopped and unloaded the victims. These locations are pin-pointed precisely at the right of the picture with the arrows. I say in advance that here they are labelled execution site 1, execution site 2. This is the correct chronology. On other pictures, we will have to -- I will have to explain the labelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next picture. 140. We see a split image of an area. One is dated 5 July. One is dated 27 July. And it's Orahovac. Is that anywhere near the Grbavci school and what you just pointed out?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just briefly, what -- what do you make of the -- this disturbed -- what you've called disturbed soil on the 27th and none on the 5th?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]

It would not be possible. Even by bringing witnesses back to the spot, it would not have been possible because they would never have recognised the place. They were taken there by night-time, and it was behind -- the first execution site is behind this railroad line, and this railroad line is on an elevation about 3 metres high. So without these technical means, we would never have been able to -- to spot these suspect sites which appear to be mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next shot. 142. We see that you've labelled this LZ which must be for "Lazete," I take it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The labelling LZ is Lazete because the first maps that we had of this area, it was not Orahovac. It was Lazete, the village of Lazete. So we named it LZ. But later on, we used the -- the wording of the imagery by naming these places Orahovac. So this picture shows the Lazete 2 site, which is, in fact, execution site 1, photographed from the elevation that is the railroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 143, the next page --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, sorry, on -- on -- on this picture, you can see -- the previous one, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Better go back to 142.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can clearly see on the ground the disturbance visible from the air where the yellow arrow points. The -- yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the situation on the ground when we did our first visit on the site, which I -- it was in April 1996. The -- this is the area where the disturbance is, so that we suspect being the execution area. And the yellow markers show the location of some of -- many items that we could see on the surface of the ground here.
